_why: Cached robots evidence for the NC anchor host, captured at P2 (the first
phase permitted to open a socket). P1 left robots.evidence_sha256 null and
the source disabled rather than author a placeholder digest.
⛔ THE HOST HAS NO robots.txt. GET /robots.txt answers HTTP 404 with a static
IIS error page. That makes the honest robots.verdict `absent`, NOT `allow` —
P0's candidates file recorded `allow`, which overstates it: nobody granted
anything, there is simply no file. `absent` is in the RobotsVerdict enum and
the guard treats it the same as allow for permission purposes, so this is a
truthfulness correction, not a behaviour change.
TWO DIGESTS, AND ONLY ONE OF THEM IS THE REGISTRY'S:
sha256_raw_404_body   — the bytes actually returned, cached beside this
file as .robots-404-body.html so a human can audit
what 'absent' meant on this date.
sha256_fetcher_visible — the digest of the DIRECTIVE TEXT, which for a
non-2xx response is the empty string. This is what
pipeline/fetch/client.ts hashes (`res.ok ? text : ''`)
and therefore the ONLY value that can appear as
robots.evidence_sha256 without the drift check
firing on every single run.
Drift semantics that follow from this, stated so nobody 'fixes' it later:
- host keeps answering 404      -> digest still e3b0c442… -> unchanged
- host PUBLISHES a robots.txt   -> digest changes         -> ingest_paused
- host answers 5xx              -> client throws (unknown is not permission)
That is the correct behaviour in all three directions.
The empty-string digest is a well-known constant and is not evidence of a
fetch having happened. The evidence of the fetch is the cached 404 body and
its own digest, both recorded below.

controls.positive: GET https://example.com/ -> HTTP 200, 559 B (the probe can see success)
controls.negative: GET https://this-host-does-not-exist-brdf-20260819.invalid/ -> curl exit 6, DNS failure (the probe can see failure)
controls.parser_negative: robots-parser on 'User-agent: *\nDisallow: /' -> isAllowed = FALSE — proves the parser can refuse, so the 'allowed' result on empty text is a real verdict and not a broken parse
